verdict.label: Full review
verdict.summary: Create a Web App or Automated App / Bot in the X Developer Console, configure OAuth 2.0 with exact-match redirect URIs, fund developer credits via pay-per-use pricing, and request fine-grained scopes.
verdict.cost: Pay-per-use credit system with no monthly fees or subscriptions; read/write actions consume credits dynamically.

composioFit.summary: X (Twitter) is NOT in Composio's toolkit catalog, requiring a custom toolkit or Composio's auth for custom tools.
whyOwnApp: X (Twitter) is not in Composio's default toolkit catalog, so you must use a custom app integration path.
Bringing your own app provides dedicated provider rate limits and specific scope configurations.

phases.name: Create Developer App
steps: Go to console.x.com and sign in with your X account.
Click New App or Create App and enter a name, description, and use case.
Generate and securely store your API Key, API Secret, Client ID, and Client Secret.
phases.handoff: Handing over your Client ID, Client Secret, and API credentials for configuration.

phases.name: Configure Authentication & Scopes
steps: Enable OAuth 2.0 in your App's authentication settings in the Developer Console.
Select your app type (e.g., Web App or Automated App / Bot for confidential clients).
Add callback URLs to your app's allowlist with exact-match validation.
Configure requested OAuth 2.0 scopes such as tweet.read, tweet.write, users.read, and offline.access.
phases.handoff: Configuring callback URLs and scopes in the developer console.

phases.name: Fund Developer Credits
steps: Purchase upfront credits in the Developer Console to cover pay-per-usage API calls.
Save an eligible payment card to claim free credit incentives.
Set up spending limits and auto-recharge rules to prevent interruptions.
phases.handoff: API credits funded and ready for test requests.

artefacts.title: OAuth 2.0 Scope Justification
artefacts.body: Scopes requested: tweet.read, tweet.write, users.read, follows.read, follows.write, offline.access. Justification: Required for the AI agent to read user timelines, post updates on behalf of authorized users, view profile data, manage follows, and maintain persistent access via refresh tokens without repeated prompts.

blockers.symptom: {"errors":[{"code":415,"message":"Callback URL not approved for this client application."}]}
blockers.cause: The callback URL passed in the request does not match the allowlist registered in the Developer Console exactly, including protocol or trailing slashes.
blockers.fix: Ensure your callback URL matches the registered allowlist exactly and is HTTP-encoded when passing as a query parameter.
blockers.fallback: Register the exact URL string in the Developer Console app settings.

blockers.cause: Exceeded the per-endpoint rate limit window.
blockers.fix: Wait until the timestamp in the x-rate-limit-reset header or implement exponential backoff.
blockers.fallback: Cache API responses locally to reduce repeated requests.

blockers.cause: The request reached the X API from an IP address not covered by your account's IP allowlist.
blockers.fix: Sign in to the Developer Console as an Administrator, open Settings -> IP allowlist, and add your server's egress IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block.
blockers.fallback: Remove all IP allowlist rules to disable enforcement entirely.

checklist.text: Sign up for a developer account at console.x.com and accept the Developer Agreement.
Create a new Developer App and select Web App or Automated App / Bot as a confidential client.
Copy and securely store your API Key, API Secret, Client ID, and Client Secret.
Enable OAuth 2.0 in the app authentication settings.
Add exact-match callback URLs (using https:// in production or http://127.0.0.1 for local dev) to your app allowlist.
Fund your developer account with prepaid credits in the Developer Console and save an eligible payment card.
Implement OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE and request offline.access for persistent refresh tokens.

uncertainties: Exact enterprise review durations and automated app approval turnaround times are not fully documented in the public X developer platform text.
Catalog integration details for X inside Composio require manual custom toolkit setup.
